notes: Narration is in the present (Rhan 2 default before Pennod 21); the hunters' story and Mali's diary at the end recycle G12–G13 past forms in dialogue.

Productive subset respected: route prepositions with SM (dros, drwy, i, o, ar, dan, heb, plus at, am, heibio i, tuag at), mewn vs yn y, and yn + NM with place names only (yng Nghaerllion, yng Nghwm Helyg). No new a/â/gyda + AM forms were added; Dafi's 'cyffwrdd â'i' is the only â.
The crown in the pool is shown in the scene and described only as 'rhywbeth aur' (coron is a Pennod 30 lexeme).
Deliberate error: Dafi's 'heb dŵr' (s-label err) is corrected by Mali in the next line ('Heb ddŵr, Dafi'), contrasting this chapter's target.
Lexicon delta adds the forms yng / ym to cy-yn-prep (yn + NM, taught here).
Myrddin's riddle 'dilyn y gwyn' (follow the white) is the chapter's hook; the stag's nature is left unexplained.
Running words 1,282 (target 1,167, window 1,050–1,284): five route stages plus the return need the room; narration was trimmed twice to stay inside the window.
Cai is not soaked or chilled here; Pennod 19 opens with its own cold, snowy hunt so that the illness follows directly.

Fluent review 2026-10-12 (docs/reviews/welsh-review-16-20-2026-10-12.md) applied: nodyn_en now separates article and preposition mutation (pont → y bont → dros y bont); A.a6 hint, C.c1 and C.c4 answer keys widened; s107 'a'i wallt e' (mawr dropped); s002 gloss made consistent in definiteness ('ar gefn ceffyl = ar geffyl', both indefinite: the review's 'ar gefn y ceffyl = ar y ceffyl' is 7 words, over the 6-word gloss limit). Review-question verdicts, all accepted unchanged: s039 'dilyn y gwyn' as a cryptic nominalisation (riddle); s002 echo pronoun after the whole noun phrase; s004 'Wff! Wff!'; s070 cyrn (antlers) beside corn (hunting horn); s102 'dau garw … un ar y tir … un yn y dŵr'; s098 'wrth droed y bryn'; s112–113 'Beth welaist ti?' / 'Dy ben di'; s150 'rhywbeth aur'; s083 'heibio i Arth' (personal-name policy).

grammar.nodyn_en: Most prepositions cause soft mutation: heb geffyl 'without a horse', ar gefn Pero, at ddrws y llys. Through y/'r the preposition adds nothing, but the article's own mutation stays: pont → y bont → dros y bont. Yn 'in' takes nasal mutation before a place name: yng Nghaerllion. Mewn means 'in a': mewn llwyn, but yn y llwyn.
